limitations: Paper full text (Blood 2022, PMC8938936) and its supplement not retrievable (PDF-only PMC record; Europe PMC fulltext 500, PDF render 403, Unpaywall/ASH PDF 403; not bypassed). Design comes from the deposited file_assignment_*.txt files, the PRIDE protocol text, MaxQuant outputs and raw headers. The cited gel method (Corso et al. 2016, PMC4878517) has its methods only in SI, not retrieved.

pYome rep1/rep2 per mix (803, 806) encoded as technical replicates of one physical SILAC mix; whether they are repeated pTyr IPs from the same lysate or re-injections of one IP is undocumented. If they were independent cultures, biological replicate numbers of the pYome rows would need to change.

Out of scope: the pYome MaxQuant search (summary.txt) also contains TO_Wilke_200418_180518_pYome_R1_277/_280 and _R2_277/_280 (experiments R1_277, R1_280, R2_277, R2_280), which are NOT deposited in PXD018961 and have no channel map in file_assignment_pYome.txt; they are not annotated. All 142 deposited raw files are annotated.

Software version conflict: PRIDE dataProcessingProtocol says MaxQuant 1.6.0.1; this matches the pYome parameters.txt, but the gProteome parameters.txt says 1.5.2.8. The precursor tolerance 6 ppm is taken from the protocol text for both searches (not recorded in the deposited MaxQuant tables).

The gProteome deposit protocol does not state reduction/alkylation reagents or gel type (left 'not available' / parent term 'Gel electrophoresis'). PRIDE's instrument/gradient text is written for the phospho-peptide samples; gProteome NCE (30) and scan range come from raw headers (one or two files per lane sampled, not all 138).

characteristics[genetic modification] is a custom characteristics column (spec 'Extending Templates'), mirrored in factor value[genetic modification]; time encodes days of doxycycline-induced shRNA expression in characteristics[sampling time].
sdrf-tools cellline lookup returned a wrong fuzzy match for BL60 (NCI-BL1339, CVCL_2637); the Cellosaurus API entry CVCL_7034 was used instead.
